topics.title: Trigonometry 2
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Determine trigonometric ratios of angles greater than 90°. (u, s)
Use the graphs of trigonometric functions to determine values of sine, cosine and tangent for any angle. (u, s)
Apply sine and cosine rules to solve real life problems. (k, u, s)

body.text: Trigonometric ratios extend beyond the 0°-90° range covered by right-angled triangles: sin(150°) = sin(30°) = 0.5, and cos(120°) = -cos(60°) = -0.5. The graphs of sine and cosine repeat every 360° and oscillate between -1 and 1, which is how a calculator or graph gives values for any angle, including negative and reflex angles.

For triangles that are not right-angled, the sine rule relates each side to the sine of its opposite angle, and the cosine rule relates all three sides to one angle. The sine rule: a/sin(A) = b/sin(B) = c/sin(C). The cosine rule: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab cos(C).

body.latex: \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C}, \qquad c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C

body.text: Two poles, 8.3 m and 11.5 m long, are placed with one end of each touching, and their far ends 4.7 m apart. Using the cosine rule to find the angle θ between the poles: 4.7^2 = 8.3^2 + 11.5^2 - 2(8.3)(11.5)cos(θ), so 22.09 = 68.89 + 132.25 - 190.9cos(θ), giving cos(θ) = (68.89+132.25-22.09)/190.9 ≈ 0.943, so θ ≈ 19.4°.
